title: The Simon Commission, 1928

endcard.line: Pictures: Punjab State archives (public domain); unknown (British India) (CC0)

segments.say: In nineteen twenty-seven, Britain decided to send a commission to decide India's political future. Its seven members did not include a single Indian.
When it landed in Bombay on the third of February nineteen twenty-eight, it was met by protests and banners that said: Simon, go back.
The Congress had already resolved to boycott it, in December nineteen twenty-seven. A section of the Muslim League joined the boycott too.
In Lahore, Lala Lajpat Rai led a march against the commission. The police charged it with lathis, and he was badly hurt.
He died on the seventeenth of November. A month later, Bhagat Singh, Azad and Rajguru shot dead Saunders, a police officer involved in the lathi-charge.
So a commission meant to settle India's future instead united its critics, and sharpened the demand for self-rule.
For GS One, link the Simon Commission to the boycott, the Lahore lathi-charge, and the radical turn that followed.

sources: NCERT Class 8, Our Pasts III, ch. 8 (hess208, read): in 1927 the British government decided to send a commission headed by Lord Simon to decide India's political future; met with demonstrations and banners saying 'Simon Go Back'; on 17 December 1928 Bhagat Singh, Azad and Rajguru assassinated Saunders, a police officer involved in the lathi-charge that caused the death of Lala Lajpat Rai

Wikipedia, 'Simon Commission' (read): seven members of the British Parliament under John Simon; no Indian members; Congress resolved to boycott at its December 1927 Madras session; a Muslim League faction also boycotted; arrived in Bombay on 3 February 1928 to protests; Lajpat Rai led a protest in Lahore, was beaten by police and died on 17 November 1928

quiz.q: Why was the Simon Commission boycotted?
options: It was led by an Indian
quiz.why: All seven members were British MPs.

quiz.q: Where did Lala Lajpat Rai lead the march against the Commission?
The Simon Commission arrived in India in…
quiz.why: It reached Bombay on 3 February 1928; the decision to send it was taken in 1927.
